questions.title: Marathon Multi-Segment Vector Displacement and Bearing

cognitive_classification.crux_move: Sum sequential orthogonal 2D displacement vectors into net Cartesian coordinates (5, 3) and evaluate Euclidean norm

questions.stem: During a Marathon race, Aditya runs 3 km towards East. He then turns right and runs 5 km and then turns left and runs 4 km. He again turns left and runs 8 km. Finally, he turns left and runs 2 km to reach the finishing point. How far and in which direction is he now from the starting point?

hint_ladder.hint1_conceptual_nudge: Represent each leg of Aditya's path as a Cartesian coordinate vector (dx, dy), taking East as +x and North as +y.
hint_ladder.hint2_tactical_step: Compute net x = 3 + 4 - 2 = 5 km, and net y = -5 + 8 = 3 km. Use the distance formula d = √(x² + y²).

solution.derivation: Assign starting point at (0, 0). Vector moves: 3 km East -> (3, 0); right 5 km (South) -> (3, -5); left 4 km (East) -> (7, -5); left 8 km (North) -> (7, 3); left 2 km (West) -> (5, 3). Net displacement vector is (5, 3). Distance = √(5² + 3²) = √(25 + 9) = √34 km. Since x > 0 and y > 0, direction is North-East.

independent_check.verification: Net horizontal = 3 + 4 - 2 = 5 km (East); Net vertical = -5 + 8 = +3 km (North). Distance √(25+9)=√34 km, direction North-East. Matches Option D uniquely.

distractor_rationale.A: Confused radical notation and neglected sign cancellation on vertical components.
distractor_rationale.B: Inverted final net displacement direction to South-West while keeping correct magnitude.
distractor_rationale.C: Preserved South bearing from intermediate step 2 instead of resolving final positive y-coordinate.

questions.stem: If p + q + r = 0, then the value of (q + r)²/(qr) + (p + r)²/(pr) + (p + q)²/(pq) is:

hint_ladder.hint1_conceptual_nudge: Since p + q + r = 0, substitute q + r = -p, p + r = -q, and p + q = -r into the numerators.

The expression becomes: p²/(qr) + q²/(pr) + r²/(pq) = (p³ + q³ + r³)/(pqr). From the fundamental identity, if p + q + r = 0, then p³ + q³ + r³ = 3pqr. Therefore, the expression equals 3pqr / pqr = 3.

questions.title: Dual Sphere Radii Reconstruction and Surface Area Differential

cognitive_classification.crux_move: Extract radius ratio r₁/r₂ = ∛(216/125) = 6/5, solve system with r₁+r₂=11, and evaluate 4π(r₁² - r₂²)

hint_ladder.hint1_conceptual_nudge: Sphere volume is proportional to the cube of the radius: V₁/V₂ = (r₁/r₂)³. Take the cube root of 216/125.
hint_ladder.hint2_tactical_step: r₁/r₂ = 6/5. Since r₁ + r₂ = 11, find r₁ and r₂. Then compute ΔA = 4π(r₁² - r₂²).

solution.derivation: Volume ratio V₁/V₂ = r₁³/r₂³ = 216/125 => r₁/r₂ = ∛216 / ∛125 = 6/5. Let r₁ = 6k, r₂ = 5k. Sum of radii: 6k + 5k = 11k = 11 cm => k = 1. Thus r₁ = 6 cm and r₂ = 5 cm. Total surface area difference: ΔA = 4πr₁² - 4πr₂² = 4π(6² - 5²) = 4π(36 - 25) = 4π(11) = 44π cm². Using π = 3.14: ΔA = 44 × 3.14 = 138.16 cm².

independent_check.verification: 4 × 3.14 × 11 = 138.16 cm². V₁/V₂ = 6³/5³ = 216/125. Exact match to Option B.

distractor_rationale.A: Transposed digits 138.16 to 183.16.
distractor_rationale.C: Computed linear radius difference times π: 3.14 × 11 = 34.54.
distractor_rationale.D: Added the surface areas instead of subtracting.

questions.title: Dual Circle Theorem Proof: Parallel Chord Radius and Intersecting Circle Cyclic Quadrilateral Parallels

cognitive_classification.crux_move: Prove Statement I via Pythagorean radius r² = 4² + 3² = 25 => d₂ = √(25 - 16) = 3 cm; Prove Statement II via exterior angle of inscribed cyclic quadrilateral ABFE equaling interior opposite ∠C

questions.stem: Read the given statements carefully and select the correct option: Statement-I: The lengths of two parallel chords of a circle are 6 cm and 8 cm. If the smaller chord is at distance 4 cm from the centre, then the distance of the other chord from the centre is 3 cm. Statement-II: In the given figure (not drawn to scale), ABCD is a cyclic quadrilateral. A circle passing through A and B meets AD and BC in the points E and F respectively. Then EF || DC.

options.A: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are true.
options.B: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are false.
options.C: Statement-I is true but Statement-II is false.
options.D: Statement-I is false but Statement-II is true.

answer.value: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are true.

hint_ladder.hint1_conceptual_nudge: For Statement-I, perpendicular from the centre bisects the chord. Use Pythagoras to find the radius r, then find the distance of the 8 cm chord.
hint_ladder.hint2_tactical_step: Statement-I: Half-chords are 3 cm and 4 cm. r² = 3² + 4² = 25 => r = 5. Distance d = √(5² - 4²) = 3 cm (True). Statement-II: ABFE is cyclic => ∠BFE = 180° - ∠A. ABCD is cyclic => ∠C = 180° - ∠A. Since ∠BFE = ∠C, EF || DC (True).

solution.derivation: Proof of Statement-I: Let the circle have radius r. The perpendicular from the centre to a chord bisects the chord. For the chord of length 6 cm: half-length = 3 cm, distance from centre = 4 cm. By Pythagorean theorem: r² = 3² + 4² = 9 + 16 = 25 => r = 5 cm. For the other parallel chord of length 8 cm: half-length = 4 cm. Its distance d from the centre satisfies: d² + 4² = r² = 25 => d² = 25 - 16 = 9 => d = 3 cm. Thus, Statement-I is TRUE. Proof of Statement-II: Quadrilateral ABFE is cyclic (vertices A, B, F, E all lie on the inner circle). In a cyclic quadrilateral, the sum of opposite angles is 180°: ∠A + ∠EFB = 180° => ∠EFB = 180° - ∠A. Quadrilateral ABCD is also cyclic (vertices A, B, C, D lie on the outer circle). Hence: ∠A + ∠C = 180° => ∠C = 180° - ∠A. Comparing the two equations: ∠EFB = ∠C. But ∠EFB and ∠C are corresponding angles for lines EF and DC intersected by transversal line BC. Since the corresponding angles are equal, line EF must be parallel to line DC (EF || DC). Thus, Statement-II is TRUE. Therefore, Both Statement-I and Statement-II are true, corresponding to Option A.

independent_check.verification: Statement-I: d = √(5² - 4²) = 3 cm (Exact). Statement-II: ∠EFB = ∠C = 180° - ∠A => EF || DC by corresponding angles converse theorem. Both statements are rigorously proved true. Option A is exact.

distractor_rationale.B: Falsely rejected both mathematical proofs.
distractor_rationale.C: Accepted Statement-I calculation but failed to deduce the parallel cyclic angle theorem for Statement-II.
distractor_rationale.D: Falsely claimed Statement-I chord calculation was invalid.
